To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a biphasic system with polyvinyl alcohol as stabilising agent for benzaldehyde lyases allows for a stable continuous operation with superior productivity and product purity.
the entrapment of enzymes into polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) beads allows for continuous production of (R) -3,3'furoin in a fluidised-bed reactor.
the entrapment of benzaldehyde lyases in polymer beads enables the stable operation in biphasic reaction media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of new biocatalytic processes for the production of enantiopur chiral compounds.
the development of continuous processes for the improved synthesis with enzymes.
the synthesis of enantiomerically pure (R) 2,2'-furoin in a continuous process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entrapment of benzaldehyde lyas in PVA beads allows for continuous operation in a biphasic system of water and toluene with a productivity of 0.4 mmol L(-1) h(-1).
the use of a polymer-entrapped enzyme in a fluidised-bed reactor is a promising approach for continuous production of chiral hydrophobic products.
the entrapment of enzymes in polymer beads enables continuous operation of the enzyme in a biphasic reaction system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of enzyme stabilisation and biphasic operation is an efficient strategy for the improved synthesis in organic solvents of chiral compounds with low solubility in water.
this concept can be used to improve the synthesis of hydrophobic compounds in a biphasic system by using a hydrophobic enzyme in a fluidised bead reactor.
the entrapment in polyvinyl alcohol beads enables a stable and continuous synthesis of enantioselective products in a non aqueous environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
enzyme catalysed biphasic reaction processes can be operated in a continuous manner with improved stability of the enzymes and high productivities.
the combination of enzyme stabilising polymeric beads and a fluidised bed bioreactor enables the stable operation of a biocatalyst in an organic solvent.
the use of polymer beads is not limited to the stabilisation of enzymes in aqueous biphasic reaction conditions, but also allows for the operation of enzymes in non-aqueous reaction systems.
